title: MessagePlanV1dot1
description: K-03 v1.1, a minor version of the composer's message plan and slots (T-1104; QUESTIONS.md CQ-82; DECISIONS.md DL-145; contracts/message-plan/README.md section 'v1.1'). It only adds to v1 (message-plan.v1.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here): every v1 definition is here under its own name, the unchanged ones by reference, so every v1 document is a v1.1 document. composeInput is restated so that each of its facts is a slot fact (v1's fact) or a term fact (termFact): one of Rosie's own fixed terms that the step's card states, such as S1-02's setup time and Rosie's $2 fee, with its source line (RULES 3.15; arch 12 line 592: Rosie's own fee terms stay words, not slots). So a plan may state such a term and arch 07 line 403 ('Only <facts> may be stated') still holds. inputAndPlan pairs an input with the plan made from it, for the named rule numbersHeldByFacts (message-plan.rules.mjs). The plan, the model's structured output, is v1's exactly; so are the slots, the plan an outbox row stores, the final parts and the check result. Owner: the architect.

termFact.title: TermFact
termFact.description: One of Rosie's own fixed terms that the step's card states, given to the composer as a fact so that a plan may state it in words (v1.1, T-1104; CQ-82; arch 07 line 403: only <facts> may be stated). For S1-02: the setup times, free to use, and Rosie's $2 fee (RULES 3.15). It is not a slot: the compiler turns the sample cast's values into slots, except Rosie's own fee terms (arch 12 line 592), and a term is the same for every business. Nor is it the fee slot, which is the business's own late-cancel and no-show fee (RULES 3.3); Rosie's own fee is never part of the price (RULES 3.14). Code copies it word for word from the step's card in the bundle (K-01 step say[].elements.card.lines) when it builds the row's input; the composer states it in its words or leaves it out, never as a slot; the slot filler fills nothing from it (C-088).

value.description: The term's words exactly as the step's card states them for this business, such as 'About 15 minutes for your first kind of work' or '$2 a booking, counted at its check-in or DONE, explained before you go live' (S1-02's card; MASTER-FLOW-A.md line 28). With the no-$2 switch on, the card's $2 line reads as that switch says (RULES 3.15; K-01 record.switches.no2). The composer's literal check and the Values check read it as they read any fact's value (README 'v1.1').

source.description: The source line of the term: the step's card line it is copied from and, where one sets the term, the rule, such as 'S1-02's card, line 4 (...); RULES 3.15' (CQ-82: each term with its source line; 02-contracts section 2 item 4).

inputFact.title: InputFact
inputFact.description: One fact of the composer's input (v1.1; CQ-82): a slot fact, a slot name and its value (v1's fact), or a term fact (termFact). The two never overlap: a slot fact has a slot and no source, a term fact a source and no slot.

composeInput.title: ComposeInput
composeInput.description: The composer's input, one per outbox row (arch 07 line 397; 02-contracts K-03 'The composer's input'), given to the model as tagged inputs, long ones first: <conversation>, <master_text>, <facts>, <audience>, <language>, <channel>, <situation>, <allowed_formats>, <allowed_links>, then <inbound>. v1.1 (T-1104; CQ-82) changes only facts: each is a slot fact or a term fact (inputFact), so every v1 input is a v1.1 input. It carries the committed choices and only what limit 7 lets the recipient see, never the frontier (arch 07 line 397): no other field is allowed (v1's refuse-frontier-in-input). The Tool API's compose input serves it (K-09).

row.description: The outbox row this plan is for: one message to one recipient on one channel (arch 07 line 397; 02-contracts K-04 outbox rows).

turn.description: The turn that committed the row (arch 02 line 121; CQ-09).

conversation.description: <conversation>: the reader's last 6 messages with this business, redacted (arch 07 line 397). That there are at most 6 is a code check.

facts.description: <facts>: only what limit 7 lets this reader see (arch 07 lines 397, 403; arch 06 line 311), each a slot fact, a slot name and its value (v1), or a term fact, one of Rosie's own fixed terms the step's card states, with its source line (v1.1; CQ-82). The composer's literal check (C-118) and the Values check (C-092) read every fact's value, slot facts' and term facts' alike (README 'v1.1').

allowedFormats.description: <allowed_formats>: what this phone allows right now, from the channel, whether the chat exists and the step's elements (arch 07 line 365; C-128).

allowedLinks.description: <allowed_links>: the link slots this message may carry (arch 07 line 397; 02-contracts K-03 'links').

options.description: The open question's options, in order, with their labels (arch 07 line 365: 'the step's elements'; K-01 elements.buttons). Empty when the step asks nothing with options.

pageTypes.description: The page types the step allows (K-01 step pageTypes; arch 01 line 97; arch 07 line 365: 'the step's page types'). Free strings until K-21 (CQ-16).

items.description: One page type (K-01 step pageTypes; CQ-16).

openQuestions.description: The questions still open with this reader, for a threaded reply (arch 07 line 389). Empty when none is open.

inbound.description: <inbound>, only in a reply to its sender; else null (arch 07 line 397).

inputAndPlan.title: InputAndPlan
inputAndPlan.description: A composer input and the plan made from it, side by side (v1.1, T-1104), so that the named rule numbersHeldByFacts (message-plan.rules.mjs) can hold across the two what one JSON Schema cannot: every number the plan states outside its slots is held by a fact of the input (arch 07 lines 403, 409; README 'Named rule (v1.1)'). A form for fixtures, as K-02's contextAndDecide pairs a context with its decide result: at run time the composer (C-118) and the message checks (C-092) read the two apart, and nothing stores or sends the pair.
